title: Comparison of Wave Functions
description: Essential Criteria: The response must correctly state that the wave functions for the singly-ionized helium atom are similar to those of the hydrogen atom with the appropriate modifications for the nucleus charge.

title: Combining Spin and Wave Functions
description: Essential Criteria: The response must explain how to combine the spatial wave functions and spin functions to form a total eigenfunction of definite spin.

title: Two-Electron Wave Function
description: Important Criteria: The response should provide a valid two-electron wave function that incorporates both spatial and spin components.

title: Total Spin Calculation
description: Important Criteria: The response must correctly identify the total spin of the provided two-electron wave function.

title: Pauli Exclusion Principle
description: Important Criteria: The response should demonstrate that the chosen wave function adheres to the Pauli exclusion principle by showing that identical states lead to a vanishing wave function.

title: Antisymmetry Check
description: Important Criteria: The response must show that the wave function is antisymmetric with respect to the exchange of the two electrons.

title: Sign Mistakes
description: Pitfall Criteria: The response should avoid common errors such as incorrect signs in the wave function expressions.

title: Missing Factors
description: Pitfall Criteria: The response should ensure that normalization factors, such as 1/sqrt(2), are included where necessary.
